what_happened: The job was meant to make the decisions page show only open proposals that are above the raising role's limit. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict with one major finding and no blocker. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet and no checks are listed as failed. The finding: approved and rejected proposals were still showing on the published page. The job did not find, fix or name the root cause. For decided proposals it only moved an existing filter in `read_snapshot()` and `render()` in xtask/src/decisions.rs, and the changelog claimed more than that.
cause: The request and reading described the wanted page content but did not require a diagnosis: why decided proposals reach the published page, from which data source and state. Without a criterion for the root cause and a test that uses real decided proposals, the producer can pass by shifting a filter. Athena's checks run only on the final tree, so the producer is not asked to show the cause or to show the bug reproduced before the fix. A summary or changelog that claims more than the diff does is caught only at the final verdict. The owner-facing page area has already been rejected repeatedly because work was not checked against real proposals.
prevention: For any job that fixes wrong output, the reading must include a criterion that names the root cause: where the wrong items enter and why they are not excluded. It must also require a test built from real decided (approved and rejected) proposals. That test must show the items are absent from the rendered page and must fail on the old code, with the failing run recorded in a place the verifier can see. The producer must state the cause in its report, and the changelog must say only what the diff does.
proposed_request: Fix the decisions page so it shows only proposals that are open and above the raising role's limit. Approved and rejected proposals must never appear on the published page. First find out why decided proposals reach the page today: trace how xtask/src/decisions.rs read_snapshot() and render() choose proposals, and which proposal states and data sources let decided ones through. State that cause in the changelog entry. Fix it at the cause, not by moving an existing filter. Acceptance: (1) a test uses fixtures of approved, rejected, open-above-limit and open-below-limit proposals, taken from the real record shapes, and the rendered page contains only the open above-limit ones; (2) the check output shows this test failing on the old code and passing on the new code; (3) the changelog says only what the diff changes; (4) run the renderer over the current real proposals and confirm that no decided proposal is on the page.
